lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The envelope was thin and honest. The numbers inside were too. The exams didn’t clear the bar. It didn’t matter how carefully you organized the documents, how sincerely you wrote your letter, or how neat your file looked when it slid across the desk.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Rules don’t bend for effort. They don’t negotiate with intention. The result was simple: not this year.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Maybe you did it clean. Maybe you never cut corners. That matters, just not to a score sheet. Not today.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: So you put the notes back on the shelf, not as trophies of failure but as a map. You mark the topics that hurt, the hours that weren’t enough, the places where guessing disguised itself as hope.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Next year is not a consolation prize. It is a second chance that begins now. The calendar will circle back, and when it does, you’ll meet it with steadier hands.
